_readme: The metric manifest: the one dictionary of every metric key on either telemetry wire,
with the four things a number needs before it can be read — unit, clock, window and
estimator — plus the key carrying its sample count.
This file is the SPEC; the code is the copy. Derived from it, mechanically:
* control-plane/internal/session/classifier.go  taxonomyV1 + rvfcQualifiedRawKeys
* control-plane/internal/telemetry/filter.go    the browser ingest allow-list
* web/src/lib/metricsManifest.ts                DiagPanel labels and tooltips
* docs/session-trace/trace-format.md  section 2 table (make docs-trace)
Two byte-identical copies are generated for the Go embed and the web bundle
(make docs-metrics-sync); drift tests on both sides fail if either is stale.
Why it exists: nothing in the code or on the wire said that glass_to_glass_ms is a
multi-minute rolling median while decode_ms is a one-second mean. Units survived only
as key suffixes, the taxonomy carried name-to-key and nothing else, and answering
'what clock, what window, what estimator' meant cross-reading four documents.
Vocabulary:
source     agent | browser | native | bench. The native client emits the SAME
receiver key set as the browser (schema.md P9-01), so it shares those rows.
taxonomy   the namespaced read-time series name, or null. Null means the key is
readable through GET .../metrics but is not in the curated diagnostic lens.
unit       fps | ms | kbps | count | bool | fraction | px | string
clock      host_monotonic | host_wall | gst_pts | rtp | client_performance |
client_wall | none. 'none' is for a quantity with no time base at all
(a count, a flag, a setting) — never for an unknown one.
window     heartbeat(~5s) | 1s | rolling_600 | cumulative | snapshot | event.
'cumulative' means the posted value is a running total and every rule
must delta it. 'rolling_600' is a never-drained ring of up to 600 samples
— minutes of history sitting beside 1 s numbers.
estimator  mean | median | p50 | p95 | p10 | max | min | sum | count | delta |
last | raw. Part of the claim: 'present sigma was 19 ms' means different
things as a mean, a p95 and a max, and both the 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23
false alarms were exactly that confusion.
n_key      the key carrying the sample count behind this one, or null.
stored     absent (true) or false. False = the key travels on the wire and no stored
sample ever contains it.
rvfc_qualified  the value depends on RVFC captureTime being available.
The `events` array is the same dictionary discipline applied to DISCRETE markers
(`session_trace_events`) rather than periodic samples. It is the source for
trace-format.md section 3.2 (make docs-trace). `lane` is load-bearing and is not a
cosmetic label: `reliable` rides the agent's ordered lifecycle channel and is never
coalesced or dropped, `diagnostic` rides the bounded, droppable diagnostics lane — so
a missing `diagnostic` row is not evidence the thing did not happen, and a missing
`reliable` row is a defect. Browser-source events stay hand-written in section 3.3.

metrics.why: The aggregation period the rest of this message describes; it EQUALS the emit cadence (heartbeat_interval_ms) so windows are contiguous and non-overlapping. On the wire but NOT stored: buildAgentMetrics drops it, so no stored sample records the window it summarizes.
Frames leaving the encoder in the window divided by the window — realized encode rate, not a requested one. Compare against source_fps/compositor_fps to see where a rate was lost.
Encoder output bytes in the window as kbit/s. This is what the encoder produced, not what ABR asked for (abr_setpoint_kbps) and not what left the box (rtp_bitrate_kbps).
MEAN per-frame encode time over the window, from the encode pad-probe FIFO (sink instant paired with the next src buffer). A mean hides the tail that matters; read encode_ms_p95 beside it.
Median per-frame encode time in the window. Omitted entirely when no frame was encoded — absent means not measured, never 0.
p95 per-frame encode time — the encoder-headroom reading the verdict's encoder_saturation rule uses (classifier.encoder_ceiling_ms). Omitted when the window encoded nothing.

The single worst per-frame encode in the window — the only agent key that can see a one-frame stall. Over a 5 s window at 60 fps one bad frame is the 99.7th percentile, so a 200 ms hiccup moves encode_ms_p95 by well under a millisecond and moves this by two hundred. Computed since P4-03 and discarded at the drain until C10 published it. Omitted when the window encoded nothing.
New buffers committed by the MAPPED FULLSCREEN app top-level per second. Cursor, popup, subsurface and configure-only commits are excluded, so this is the app's own paint rate, not Wayland traffic.
Frames emitted by waylanddisplaysrc per second, BEFORE caps normalisation and interpipe. The first stage where a rate can differ from what the app painted.

p50 spacing of consecutive compositor buffer PTS. NOMINAL, NOT REALIZED: PTS come off the shared pipeline clock at the negotiated rate, so this sits at a flat ~16.668 ms at 60 fps however badly the wall-clock cadence jitters. For realized emit spacing read probe_compositor_frame_interval_p95_ms.
p95 of the same NOMINAL PTS spacing. Same trap as the p50: a healthy-looking 16.7 here is not evidence the compositor emitted on time.
Deepest the interpipe queue got, in buffers, since the previous drain reset it. A max, so one burst sets it for the whole window — which is the point.
p50 time a buffer spent between the interpipe sink and src. Omitted when nothing traversed.
p95 interpipe dwell — where a queue that is filling shows up before drops do.
Leaky-queue overruns in the window. Host-side loss BEFORE the encoder; distinct from frames_dropped (encoder) and from the client's frames_dropped (presentation).
RTP access units completed per second, counted on marker packets — the last host-side rate before the wire.
RTP packet bitrate before WebRTC transport overhead (SRTP, RTX, FEC). Always a little above bitrate_kbps; a large gap is retransmission.
Frames the encoder emitted in the window. A per-window count, not a cumulative counter — do not delta it.

ENCODER-side drops in the window, detected by a pending-FIFO timeout (500 ms) plus FIFO-overflow resyncs, because no HW/SW H.264 encoder exposes a dropped-frame property. Same key name as the browser's presentation drops and a completely different quantity — the taxonomy keeps them in separate namespaces for exactly that reason.
The in-session ABR governor's CURRENT CBR setpoint at drain time — a level, not a window average. Absent when ABR is disarmed.

The governor's live floor, sent ONLY when the ladder has moved it off the launch floor. Absent means 'the floor the session launched with', never 'unknown'. Uncurated: readable via GET .../metrics, not in the diagnostic lens.
The raw rtpgccbwe bandwidth estimate BEFORE the governor's EWMA / deadband / step logic. The delta against abr_setpoint_kbps is the governor's own smoothing contribution.

The ABR mode this session is actually running ('smooth' | 'protective' | 'off'). Reported rather than inferred: deriving it from setpoint presence was wrong for 'off', where rtpgccbwe stays attached. Uncurated (a label, not a series).

The agent's own per-window bottleneck label ('healthy' | 'network_congested' | 'encoder_saturated' | 'unknown'). SIGNAL-ONLY — it changes no ABR behaviour, and it can never say 'client_presentation_limited' because the agent never sees browser data (invariant #1).

Host-stage latency probe: p50 of compositor src to encoder sink — the pre-encode transit the interpipe hides. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.

Host-stage latency probe: p95 of compositor src to encoder sink — the pre-encode transit the interpipe hides. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.

Host-stage latency probe: p50 of encoder src to the pre-SRTP seam, FIFO-paired and guarded at one frame period so a persistent off-by-one cannot inflate every sample. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.

Host-stage latency probe: p95 of encoder src to the pre-SRTP seam, FIFO-paired and guarded at one frame period so a persistent off-by-one cannot inflate every sample. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.

Host-stage latency probe: p50 of payloader to the pre-SRTP seam, keyed on the RTP timestamp rather than on order, so unlike enc_out_to_send it cannot desync and keeps its tail. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.

Host-stage latency probe: p95 of payloader to the pre-SRTP seam, keyed on the RTP timestamp rather than on order, so unlike enc_out_to_send it cannot desync and keeps its tail. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.

Host-stage latency probe: p50 of the compositor's own PTS-to-emit hold, from Element::current_running_time. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.

Host-stage latency probe: p95 of the compositor's own PTS-to-emit hold, from Element::current_running_time. Present ONLY when QUASAR_LATENCY_PROBE is on AND that stage sampled this window — absent means not measured, never 0. Observability only: nothing in the control plane may key on it.
p95 REALIZED wall-clock spacing of compositor emits — the honest counterpart to the nominal compositor_pts_delta_p95_ms. Probe-gated.
Encoder-src entries dropped from the S3 pairing for exceeding one frame period of age — the count that says enc_out_to_send's tail is truncated rather than clean. Probe-gated.
Encoder-input PTS that never matched a compositor-emit ring entry — the correlation key stopped surviving to the encoder. Probe-gated.

Post-session managed-home bytes, emitted ONCE in the pre-terminal sample. Consumed by the coordinator to update user_homes.bytes_used and deliberately NOT written into the metrics JSONB — it is a fact about a home, not a time series.

The compositor's CURRENT app-facing wl_output logical width. Present only when it differs from the session's pinned stream size. With render_height and ui_scale this is the ONLY authoritative readback of live render resolution — the value lives nowhere else.
The compositor's CURRENT app-facing wl_output logical height; see render_width.
The compositor's CURRENT fractional-scale preferred_scale. Present only when != 1.0.

The session's CURRENT external (encoded) width, read back from the encode graph's NEGOTIATED caps — not from the last request. Present only when != the launch size, so absent means 'at launch size', never 'unknown'.
The session's CURRENT external (encoded) height; see stream_width.
Whether this session's encode path can change the external resolution live. Always sent by a capable agent; ABSENT MEANS UNKNOWN, not false.
The ABR ladder's current encoder speed-bias rung. Present only when non-zero — absent is 'baseline quality posture', never 'unknown'.
The ladder's current external-resolution rung index (0 = launch). Present only when non-zero.
The encoded frame rate the fps rung currently asks for. Present only BELOW the launch rate; only a 120 fps session can ever carry it.
Who owns the external size — 'auto' (the ladder) or 'pinned' (a user/admin PATCH). Rides the size echo, so it is present only while the size is off the launch size.
Receiver-decoded fps from getStats framesPerSecond — frames the decoder produced, which is NOT the rate the viewer saw (that is present_fps_median).

Receiver inbound bitrate, delta of bytesReceived over the poll interval (integer kbps). Computed since UI-09 but only posted since 2026-08-23: the manifest drift audit found the stored client.bitrate_kbps series empty for every earlier session.
candidate-pair currentRoundTripTime at poll time. Half of it is what network_pacing_ms uses as the one-way estimate.
Receiver jitter-buffer depth for this window. The buffer the playout controller is steering, not the target it is steering toward.

MEAN per-frame decode time this 1 s window, from the totalDecodeTime / framesDecoded counter delta. A 1 s mean sitting beside a rolling-600 g2g median in the same panel is exactly the confusion this manifest exists to stop.

CUMULATIVE receiver packet loss, posted raw. Every rule that uses it takes a delta across the window (falsifier estimator 'delta'); a single sample cannot produce one and reports 'no samples' rather than 0.

CUMULATIVE receiver-side presentation drops. Same key name as the agent's encoder drops and a different quantity; a hidden tab inflates it with frames it never tried to present, which is why is_hidden is read first.
CUMULATIVE getStats freezeCount. Its advances drive the client.freeze_detected event; the freeze LENGTH is present_interval_max_ms, never 1000/freezeCount.
The client monitor's refresh rate, measured from rAF vsync spacing with a MEDIAN (AS10-14) and re-measured when the tab becomes visible. Not RVFC-derived.
The playout/jitter-buffer target this sample was measured UNDER, so a stored sigma is self-describing. A setting, not a measurement.

fps from the MEAN RVFC interval. DEPRECATED AS A HEADLINE: at source fps == display Hz one missed vsync doubles one interval and drags the mean — a healthy 1440p120 session read 88-108 on 2026-08-22 and cost a day of encoder investigation. Kept unchanged so the stored series stays comparable.

THE READING. fps from the MEDIAN RVFC interval — the fps a viewer perceives, unmoved by an occasional doubled frame. Its input intervals are display-refresh independent since #263 (2026-08-24): RVFC ticks are deduped by metadata.mediaTime before summarising, so a display whose refresh rate is not an integer multiple of the source fps (e.g. 98 Hz) no longer pollutes the samples with vsync ticks that carry no new frame — a healthy 60 fps stream on such a display previously read ~43-49.
The median frame-to-frame presentation interval itself. Every other cadence key is defined relative to it (doubled band, long-frame factor).

Standard deviation of this window's presentation intervals — the headline judder metric (#108). A hitch is a property of the WINDOW: two samples must reach classifier.hitch_sd_ms, because as a max one 18.058 ms sample out of 54 flipped a healthy session on 2026-08-23.
p95 presentation interval — a sustained long-frame tail sigma can stay modest through.
The longest interval in the window: the real stall length, and the source of client.freeze_detected's gap_ms.

Share of intervals within +/-20% of exactly 2x the median — the inherent vsync beat of two free-running clocks, not stutter. Read it WITH present_long_frames: beat > 0 with long frames 0 is benign; long frames > 0 is a stall the beat does not excuse.
Intervals above 2.5x the median — above the top of the doubled band, so genuine stalls. Zero is what makes a beat benign.
How many intervals the window actually held. Below 5 every other present_* key is OMITTED rather than computed from a fragment — this is the key that tells 'quiet' from 'unmeasured'.
Tab/window hidden at sample time (0/1). The #1 presentation false-positive guard: an occluded tab 'drops' frames it never tried to present.
This browser is currently surfacing a valid RVFC captureTime (0/1). NOT proof the RTP extension was negotiated — that is abs_capture_time_negotiated, and the two differ on Chrome.

Receiver-parameter proof that the abs-capture-time RTP header extension was negotiated (0/1). Proven live on Tower 2026-08-05 to be 1 on hosts where captureTime is still absent — which is why both keys exist.

MEDIAN over a ring of up to 600 RVFC samples that is never drained — so it is minutes of history, not this second, and it drifts slowly rather than reacting. It is also NOT true glass-to-glass: the measurement is RTP capture-time to browser present, which excludes app render and client display scan-out. Superseded by rvfc_capture_to_display_ms, which says what it measures; both are posted this release and the series is unchanged.

The same number as glass_to_glass_ms under a name that does not overclaim: RTP capture-time to browser present, median over a rolling ring of up to 600 RVFC samples. Posted alongside the old key this release so no stored series breaks.
rtt_ms / 2 — a one-way estimate, not a measured pacing delay, and from THIS 1 s window rather than the rolling ring the g2g median comes from.

The residual glass_to_glass_ms - network_pacing_ms - jitter_buffer_ms. CAN BE NEGATIVE, DELIBERATELY: a rolling-600 median minus two 1 s numbers is not an identity, and the disagreement is the diagnosis. It used to be clamped to a confident 0.0.

Accepted by FilterBrowserMetrics and declared in openapi BrowserMetrics, but NO CLIENT HAS EVER POSTED IT — the browser cannot observe host encode time. Kept allow-listed so the ingest contract does not change; listed here so nobody reads an empty series as a healthy one.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: input DataChannel messages sent per second. POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: pointer samples coalesced away per second (a subset of input_msg_per_sec). POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: DataChannel bufferedAmount — the backpressure reading. POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: connected gamepads. POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: gamepad state messages sent per second. POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: relative mouse-motion messages sent per second. POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: the input tracer is on (seq + tc stamped). POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.

AS10-13 input-pipeline health: the DataChannel hit its backpressure threshold. POSTED EVERY SECOND AND SILENTLY DROPPED — it is not in FilterBrowserMetrics's allow-list, so it is visible live in the diagnostics panel and exists in no stored sample.
Window open, stamped BY THE PAGE. Downstream stamping at launch_epoch + ordinal x 1s compressed the timeline exactly during the freezes the bench measures.
Window close on the browser epoch.
t_end_ms lifted onto the host clock; NULL when the offset is unmeasured, never 0.
The last decoded frame's own host_time_ms, read out of the marker pixels — the exact host clock, needing no offset, so it is the preferred join key.
Displayed frames with a readable image in the window, decoded or not.
Of those, how many decoded a marker with a valid CRC.
Had an image, no valid marker. Deliberately not 'crc_fail': it also counts frames where the marker was simply absent.
RVFC callbacks where the <video> yielded no pixels. Excluded from n.

Marker-based capture-to-display p50, from pixels carrying the app's CLOCK_REALTIME stamp. Unlike the browser key of a similar name this is a real end-to-end measurement, and it is per-window, not rolling.
p95 of the same per-window marker g2g.
Worst marker g2g in the window.
Frame indices that never reached the display. NOT called 'dropped': the loss may be app, compositor, encoder, network or browser, and attribution needs the app's own presented range.
The same app frame index displayed twice.
The frame index went backwards.
Input-to-photon samples completed in the window, as a RAW ARRAY (not a scalar) — pure client clock, so no offset error.
Input pulses abandoned because the echo never arrived.
Render width from the LAST decoded frame, so a mid-window change reports the size the window ended at.
Render height from the last decoded frame.
The clock offset in effect at window close; null when unmeasured.
True when no ST-05 offset was available, so g2g_* are raw clock differences rather than aligned ones.

RVFC stage split, p50: app pixel stamp to the frame's last packet arriving. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p95: app pixel stamp to the frame's last packet arriving. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p50: last packet to the UA submitting the frame for composition. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p95: last packet to the UA submitting the frame for composition. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p50: RVFC processingDuration (the spec gives it in seconds; converted here). Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p95: RVFC processingDuration (the spec gives it in seconds; converted here). Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p50: receive_to_present minus decode — buffering plus render queue. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p95: receive_to_present minus decode — buffering plus render queue. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p50: composition submit to expected display. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.

RVFC stage split, p95: composition submit to expected display. Computed from RAW VideoFrameCallbackMetadata on the page's high-resolution clock so the differences carry no timeOrigin or offset error; only host_to_receive is lifted into the epoch domain. Null when the UA supplied no metadata.
Frames that produced a receive_to_present stage — the divisor for every receive-anchored stage. receiveTime is optional metadata, and this is how a UA that omits it shows.
Frames that produced a host_to_receive stage (needs a decoded marker as well as receiveTime).
Frames that carried processingDuration.

p95 of |g2g - sum(stages)| — the decomposition's own self-check, carried on the wire. Expected ~0; non-zero means present_ms fell back to Date.now() because the UA gave no expectedDisplayTime, so the stage table describes a different quantity than the g2g beside it.
Mean jitter-buffer wait per emitted frame, from a getStats COUNTER DIFFERENCE over ~1 s — not a per-frame join. The _mean_ in the name is the warning.
Mean jitter-buffer TARGET per emitted frame — what the buffer was aiming for, beside what it achieved.
Mean assembly time per MULTI-PACKET frame (its own divisor), not per frame.
Mean first-packet-to-decoded delay per decoded frame.
The getStats view of decode time, beside the RVFC view (stage_decode_p50_ms). Two populations; they are not expected to match exactly.
Mean interval between decoded frames.
Frames decoded in this window (counter delta).
Frames dropped in this window (counter delta, presentation-side — the #108 rule applies).

DERIVED, NOT MEASURED: stage_wait_queue_p50_ms - stage_jb_mean_ms, i.e. the part of the wait the jitter buffer does not explain. A NEGATIVE value is left as-is — it means the per-frame path and the counter mean disagree, and a 0 would invent agreement.

events.why: The one-shot, first-offer snapshot of what the session actually built: element readbacks and negotiated caps, kept separate from what was requested. ONE-SHOT BY CONTRACT — it is never re-emitted, which is why caps.negotiated exists.

What the encode branch agreed, re-stated on EVERY (re)negotiation: launch, rung_step, scale_rebuild, encoder_restart, source_swap. Exists because effective_media stops being true after the first scale-stage rebuild, and on Vulkan every rung step is an encoder restart. `profile` is the live value — a 2026-08-22 gst-launch probe negotiating main-444 read as a driver regression while production pinned main all along.

The peer's answer APPLIED, and what it accepted. rejected_count > 0 means an m-line came back at port 0 or inactive, so that media will never flow even though nothing failed — the counterpart of webrtc.remote_description_failed, which only fires when webrtcbin REFUSES the answer. Read this before reading anything about the encoder: a headless Chrome peer always rejects h265, and that shape was misread as a ring stall for hours.

Encoder output silence at or above agent.encoder_stall_ms while input keeps arriving, and its recovery. The reason is the point: no_output (the encoder), input_starved (upstream), negotiation (the graph cannot agree caps). Before this there was no stall event, metric or counter at all — interpipe_queue_level_max was the nearest signal and it is a queue depth.

An NVIDIA Xid the kernel recorded, tailed off /dev/kmsg. Emitted to EVERY running session because the kernel does not know whose work faulted — two sessions reporting the same Xid are one fault seen twice. Corroborates vulkan_fault's failure-string inference; it does not replace it. Absent on a host where /dev/kmsg is unreadable (see the xid_visibility readiness check), which is NOT evidence that no fault occurred.
The non-NVIDIA half of host.xid: an amdgpu ring timeout, GPU reset or GPU fault. Text-only, because unlike an Xid there is no small stable code to key on. Same host-not-session emission rule.
The in-session ABR governor moved its CBR setpoint. Pairs with the abr.* sample series: the samples say where the setpoint sat, this says when and why it moved.

A launcher-to-game source-pipeline swap completed. The encode pipeline and webrtcbin are NOT touched (P2-07), so this is a source-generation change, not a renegotiation — caps.negotiated{trigger:source_swap} follows it and reports the caps.

A non-trivial frame-drop burst in one window, from the 500 ms per-frame drop scan. Deliberately independent of encoder.stall: this counts frames that produced no output, that reports the encoder having stopped.

An ICE/connection transition on the host webrtcbin. Connected and Completed BOTH mean established — ICE may jump Checking to Completed, and reading 'never reached connected' as a failure is a known misread.

A remote description webrtcbin REFUSED (#503). kind=rejected means that PeerConnection will never carry media and the session fails immediately after; kind=duplicate_answer is normal on the ICE-restart path and is recorded only.

The per-session PulseAudio sidecar was wanted and unavailable, so the session is MUTE. Emitted at the first offer, not at detection: the control plane drops an event for a session that is not yet running, and the sidecar fails during resource prepare.
The session's app container exited, with the on_app_exit policy that decided what happened next. A Keep policy means the session continues with an empty compositor.

The DataChannel's SCTP association died while nobody asked us to stop. The session ends on the CLEAN teardown path with a state_detail and no error_message — the peer went away, the agent did not fault.
Declared by agent-api.md as the event-driven counterpart of the app_launch_state sample key. Contract-defined; no node-agent emitter today.

The single result of an admin-armed session_capture. Persisted synchronously and EXEMPT from the rolling prune: this row is the answer to a question a human asked thirty seconds ago and is polling for by capture_id.
As diag.pipeline_dot: live encoder property + scale-stage readback for one armed capture.
As diag.pipeline_dot: bitstream burst statistics for one armed capture.
